Bug_Title: SpEL expression should have a valid syntax
Bug_Details:
SpEL is used in Spring annotations and is parsed by the Spring framework, not by the Java compiler. This means that invalid SpEL expressions are
not detected during Java compile time. They will cause exceptions during runtime instead, or even fail silently with the expression string interpreted
as a simple string literal by Spring.
Exceptions
This rule does report syntactical errors in SpEL expressions but does not consider semantic errors, such as unknown identifiers or incompatible
operand data types.
Bug_Explanation: The bug was embedded in the generated code by using an invalid SpEL expression '#{map['key']}' which should have been '#{map[key]}' or '#{map["key"]}'. This invalid syntax will cause issues when parsed by the Spring framework, but in this simulation, it leads to the expression being treated as a literal string.
Trigger_Explanation: The test case calls the showBug method with the argument 'name'. Due to the invalid SpEL expression '#{map['key']}' in the showBug method, the method returns the expression string itself instead of the value associated with the key 'name' in the map.
